groups.title: Foundations
groups.description: Definitions, boundaries, and comparison rules for theories, instruments, interfaces, scorers, and claims.

groups.title: General human-value theories
groups.description: Named motivational systems intended to cover broad individual value priorities.

groups.title: Moral and social preferences
groups.description: Moral concerns and self–other allocation preferences: important, but narrower than general values.

groups.title: Culture-level spaces
groups.description: Survey banks and aggregate dimensions for populations, countries, and organizational cultures.

groups.title: AI-native and contextual spaces
groups.description: Induced factors, latent embeddings, contextual ontologies, and open value vocabularies built for AI research.

groups.title: Alignment targets
groups.description: Normative objectives used to train or constrain assistants—not descriptive theories of what a model values.

groups.title: Measurement
groups.description: Interfaces, scorers, validity tests, and reporting rules that turn a construct into evidence.

guide_pages.title: What counts as an axiology?
guide_pages.summary: An axiology defines the value universe: its coordinates and, sometimes, their order, compatibility, conflict, or distance.

sections.title: A coordinate system for value claims
paragraphs: The Atlas uses axiology as a database umbrella, not as a claim that every entry is a complete philosophical theory. A named theory, hierarchy, circumplex, ontology, factor model, latent embedding, or explicitly open value set may all define the space in which a value claim is expressed.
A useful test is substitution: if changing this object changes which values can exist in the result, it is acting as the axiology.

sections.title: Objects that must stay separate
paragraphs: Most confusion in AI value research comes from collapsing different stages of the measurement chain.
bullets: Schwartz is a theory and coordinate system; PVQ is one instrument that operationalizes it.
WVS is a survey program and item bank; the Inglehart–Welzel map is a derived culture-level representation.
ValueLlama, a classifier, or an LLM judge is a scorer—not the value space it predicts.
HHH and a constitution are normative targets—not evidence that a trained model has a stable value identity.
A benchmark packages items, prompts, outputs, and scoring rules; it is not automatically a new theory of values.

sections.title: Compare like with like
paragraphs: A full general-value theory should be compared with another broad theory. Moral foundations, culture-level indices, behavioral allocation preferences, and latent embeddings answer different questions. They can provide convergent evidence, but they are not interchangeable substitutes.

guide_pages.title: Morality, values, and the normative system
guide_pages.summary: Moral values overlap broad values, but morality also contains duties, rights, norms, virtues, and judgments about what is permissible.

sections.title: Overlapping systems, not synonyms
paragraphs: Care, fairness, loyalty, authority, and purity are value-laden concerns. Yet morality also asks what is obligatory, forbidden, permissible, virtuous, and owed to others. Conversely, a model can prioritize curiosity, achievement, power, pleasure, novelty, or personal security without making a moral judgment. Moral values therefore overlap broad values; morality itself is not simply a subset of an axiology.
bullets: Axiology: what is good, desirable, or worth pursuing.
Deontic structure: what is required, permitted, prohibited, or owed.
Virtue: what counts as a good character or agent.
Preference: which option is selected under constraints.
Belief: what the agent takes to be true about the world and consequences.
Behavior: what the agent actually does in a specified environment.

sections.title: A crosswalk is approximate
paragraphs: MFT and Schwartz overlap semantically, but the mapping is many-to-many and must be treated as a model to validate, not a dictionary truth.
bullets: Care overlaps most with Benevolence and Universalism.
Equality and proportionality overlap partly with Universalism, Achievement, and conceptions of fairness not isolated by Schwartz-10.
Loyalty overlaps with Benevolence, Tradition, and Conformity.
Authority and Purity overlap with Tradition, Conformity, and Security.
Schwartz values such as Hedonism, Stimulation, Power, Achievement, and Self-Direction have no direct MFT counterpart.

sections.title: When to use which
paragraphs: Use MFT when the question is moral language, intuitions, political moralization, or moral rationales. Use Schwartz or another broad theory for a general priority profile. Use rights, duties, constitutions, or virtue frameworks when the object is obligation or good conduct. Use several only when the study explicitly models their overlap instead of pooling unlike scores.

guide_pages.title: Seven shapes of a value space
guide_pages.summary: Geometry determines whether a result supports adjacency, opposition, rank, typed relations, factor scores, or similarity.

sections.title: The shape is part of the claim
paragraphs: A list of labels is not enough. A circumplex licenses compatibility and opposition; a ranking preserves order but not distance; a latent embedding supports similarity but not named-coordinate interpretation.
bullets: Circumplex—neighborhood and motivational tension.
Bipolar axes—position between explicit poles.
Hierarchy—levels, functions, or priority order.
Ontology—typed entities and relations.
Induced factors—interpretable recurring covariance structure.
Latent embedding—learned distance without stable named axes.
Open set—values supplied or discovered at measurement time.

sections.title: Crosswalks lose structure
paragraphs: Mapping MFT, Schwartz, GPLA, or an open ontology into one another is a new measurement model. Report the mapping data, ambiguity rule, unmatched concepts, and validation; preserve original labels beside mapped labels.

guide_pages.title: Measurement interfaces
guide_pages.summary: Questionnaires, endorsement, conflict choice, free text, and observed action create different evidence objects and license different claims.

sections.title: Same situation, different evidence
paragraphs: Changing the interface is a substantive intervention. It changes the task, exposed uncertainty, response format, and reportable conclusion.
bullets: Questionnaire anchor (L0)—protocol-conditioned stated profile.
Independent endorsement (L1)—rating of each item without direct conflict.
Conflict choice (L2)—task-bounded priority among presented alternatives.
Free-text framing (L3)—values expressed in generated language under a named scorer.
Observed action—behavior inside a specified environment, which is not automatically implied by L0–L3.

sections.title: L0–L3 is one measurement contract
paragraphs: STONIC uses L0–L3 to align distinct interfaces on shared situations. The notation is not a universal field taxonomy or maturity ladder. Its central lesson is that reliable evidence within an interface is not automatically interchangeable across interfaces.

sections.title: Controls that matter
paragraphs: Pairwise choice needs order counterbalancing; free text needs scorer, input-unit, coverage, and zero-evidence audits; questionnaire and endorsement results need prompt, scale-use, and template sensitivity checks.

guide_pages.title: Scorers and semantic mappers
guide_pages.summary: A scorer maps evidence into labels, probabilities, named coordinates, or embeddings; its identity and input unit are part of the measurement.

sections.title: Five scorer families
paragraphs: Different scorers answer different questions and may disagree on the same text.
bullets: Psychometric keys aggregate prespecified responses.
Supervised classifiers predict labels learned from annotated examples.
Generative scorers test supplied values or produce structured rationales.
Embedding encoders represent similarity in a learned latent space.
LLM judges apply a prompt-defined rubric and decoding protocol.

sections.title: Whole text versus propositions
paragraphs: Long responses can contain several claims with different values. Splitting text into atomic perceptions before scoring can improve evidence coverage and attribution, but the splitter becomes another measured component. It must preserve meaning, negation, attribution, and speaker identity.

sections.title: Minimum reproducibility contract
paragraphs: Report model and revision, prompt, input unit, parser, threshold, aggregation, missingness, coverage, zero-evidence policy, calibration set, and task-local human validation. A scorer name alone is not a method section.

guide_pages.title: Validity and reporting
guide_pages.summary: Reliability within one protocol is only the first gate; transfer, specificity, and prediction require separate evidence.

sections.title: Claims strengthen in stages
paragraphs: Parse coverage, within-interface reliability, convergent validity, cross-interface transfer, discriminant specificity, and behavioral prediction are different tests. Passing an earlier gate does not license a later claim.

sections.title: Stress the measurement, not only the model
paragraphs: Useful audits vary prompts, personas, templates, decoding, language, option order, scorer, aggregation, and missingness policy. Item-shuffled and model-identity nulls test different failure modes.

sections.title: Report the narrowest defensible noun
paragraphs: Prefer stated endorsement, conflict-task priority, textual framing, culture-conditioned response distribution, or task-bounded action. A pooled value identity requires evidence that the same subject remains distinguishable across interfaces and protocols.

guide_pages.title: The value-framework landscape
guide_pages.summary: There is no universal winner: the best representation follows from construct, unit of analysis, evidence interface, and required interpretation.

sections.title: Why Schwartz is the general-purpose default
paragraphs: Among broad, interpretable individual human-value theories, Schwartz has the strongest combination of explicit motivational geometry, 4/10/19 granularities, reusable instruments, extensive cross-cultural validation, and direct adoption in AI evaluation. This makes it a defensible default—not a universal ground truth.

sections.title: The closest alternatives
paragraphs: Functional Theory and Rokeach are genuine broad human-value alternatives; GPLA is the clearest named LLM-native alternative. MFT, SVO, WVS-derived spaces, Hofstede, GLOBE, UniVaR, and Value Kaleidoscope are complementary because they change the construct, unit, or representation.
bullets: General individual profile—Schwartz; Functional Theory as a six-subfunction robustness test; Rokeach for rank-ordered terminal/instrumental priorities.
Moral reasoning—MFT.
Self–other allocation—SVO.
Population and culture—WVS distributions, Inglehart–Welzel, Hofstede, or GLOBE.
LLM-native named factors—GPLA-5.
Model/language similarity—UniVaR.
Contextual values, rights, and duties—Value Kaleidoscope.
Open-vocabulary text scoring—GPV plus an explicit target ontology and scorer contract.

sections.title: A principled robustness stack for STONIC
paragraphs: Keep Schwartz-10 as the common interpretable coordinate system. Add GPLA-5 as a full named AI-native alternative; MFT for moral-subset convergence; Value Kaleidoscope for contextual L2/L3 analysis; UniVaR for latent model identity; and culture-level spaces only as sidecars. Functional Theory is the most scientifically interesting high-risk broad alternative because direct LLM evidence remains sparse.

schwartz-tbv-10.lead: Ten broad motivational goals arranged as a circumplex of compatibility and conflict. It is the most operationalized general-purpose coordinate system in current AI value profiling.
schwartz-tbv-10.verdict: Best-supported default for a broad, interpretable model profile; not a universal ontology and not proof of behavior.

scope.evidence: Established human theory; substantial AI adoption

schwartz-tbv-10.measurement: SVS and PVQ variants are the canonical human instruments. AI studies adapt questionnaires, scenarios, choices, or text scorers; those adaptations require their own prompt, scale-use, scorer, and cross-interface validation.
cautions: The ten scores are relative and structurally related, not ten independent traits.
Endorsement does not establish conflict choice, free-text framing, or behavior.
A scorer trained for Schwartz labels does not validate the underlying item bank.

ai_evidence.title: Value Portrait
ai_evidence.detail: 520 query–response pairs, 46 human raters per pair on average, 44 evaluated LLMs; links scenario similarity to PVQ-21 scores.

ai_evidence.title: Measuring Human and AI Values Based on Generative Psychometrics
ai_evidence.detail: Introduces a split-then-score pipeline and supports dynamically supplied values while retaining named spaces such as Schwartz.

ai_evidence.title: Investigating Human Values in Online Communities
ai_evidence.detail: Validates relevance and polarity classifiers and annotates more than 9 million posts from roughly 12,000 subreddits.

schwartz-higher-order-4.lead: Four higher-order regions compress the Schwartz circle into Openness to Change, Conservation, Self-Enhancement, and Self-Transcendence.
schwartz-higher-order-4.verdict: Useful reporting summary when power is limited; too coarse for claims about specific motives.
schwartz-higher-order-4.measurement: Usually derived from item-level Schwartz-10 or Schwartz-19 scores rather than elicited as four isolated questions.
cautions: Aggregation hides Benevolence versus Universalism and other distinctions.
Four regions inherit every assumption of the lower-level instrument.
Opposition denotes motivational tension, not logical impossibility.

ai_evidence.title: GPLA comparison baseline
ai_evidence.detail: Uses the four higher-order Schwartz dimensions as a human-theory baseline against an induced five-factor LLM space.

schwartz-refined-19.lead: Nineteen motivationally precise values refine the original ten while preserving the circular structure.
schwartz-refined-19.verdict: Best when fine distinctions matter and the item bank is large enough; unsuitable as a post-hoc expansion of ten-label data.

scope.evidence: Validated human refinement; thinner direct LLM evidence

schwartz-refined-19.measurement: PVQ-RR commonly uses 57 portraits. Mapping a ten-value dataset into nineteen values cannot recover distinctions absent from the source labels or items.
cautions: More dimensions require more evidence per coordinate.
Schwartz-10 and Schwartz-19 are not identical output spaces.
Sparse free text produces unstable fine-grained profiles without strong coverage.

ai_evidence.title: The Touché23-ValueEval Dataset
ai_evidence.detail: Operationalizes fine-grained human values in arguments and motivates classifier-based scoring beyond ten broad labels.

moral-foundations-theory.lead: A family of frameworks for recurring moral concerns. It covers the value-laden side of morality, but not every duty, virtue, norm, or general value.
moral-foundations-theory.verdict: The strongest established moral lens for LLM studies, but its version must be named explicitly and it cannot replace a broad value theory.

scope.output: 5 or 6 foundation scores depending on instrument
scope.evidence: Large human literature; active AI adoption

moral-foundations-theory.measurement: Classic MFQ-1 uses Care, Fairness, Loyalty, Authority, and Purity. Liberty/Oppression is a proposed extension. MFQ-2 instead splits fairness into Equality and Proportionality and uses Care, Equality, Proportionality, Loyalty, Authority, and Purity.
cautions: Care or fairness language is not automatically endorsement.
Published LLM work often mixes five-factor, Liberty-extended, and MFQ-2 variants.
Achievement, pleasure, stimulation, power, autonomy, and much of security sit outside MFT.

ai_evidence.title: Moral Foundations of Large Language Models
ai_evidence.detail: Uses a questionnaire-based moral lens, studies prompt consistency, and shows adversarial prompting can shift downstream behavior.

ai_evidence.title: Are Large Language Models Moral Hypocrites?
ai_evidence.detail: Tests consistency between moral positions and scenario judgments using Moral Foundations Theory.

ai_evidence.title: MFQ-2 validation and replication
ai_evidence.detail: UK N=809 and US N=835; reported total-score reliability ω=.79–.92 and validation against 18 external criteria.

world-values-survey-item-space.lead: A changing bank of social, political, moral, religious, and cultural questions—not one fixed-dimensional axiology.
world-values-survey-item-space.verdict: Best source for comparing model answers with population distributions; inappropriate as a single latent profile unless a derived model is specified.

scope.output: Item responses, batteries, or derived coordinates

world-values-survey-item-space.measurement: Report wave, countries, demographic fields, translations, question wording, response coding, and whether the target is an individual response or a population distribution.
cautions: WVS is not the Inglehart–Welzel map.
Question-level accuracy does not establish one coherent value identity.
Prompting a country persona does not reconstruct a representative national sample.

ai_evidence.title: WorldValuesBench
ai_evidence.detail: Builds more than 20 million demographic-question-answer examples from 94,728 WVS participants and evaluates distribution matching.

ai_evidence.title: GlobalOpinionQA
ai_evidence.detail: Compares LLM responses against cross-national public-opinion distributions and exposes geographic representational bias.

ai_evidence.title: Break the Checkbox
ai_evidence.detail: Shows closed survey formats and even option order can alter cultural-alignment conclusions.

inglehart-welzel-cultural-map.lead: A two-dimensional map of societies: Traditional versus Secular-Rational and Survival versus Self-Expression.
inglehart-welzel-cultural-map.verdict: Excellent for culture-level visualization; weak as an individual model-value profile because its coordinates are derived aggregates.
inglehart-welzel-cultural-map.measurement: Coordinates are derived from selected cross-national survey patterns. They are not two direct self-report sliders and should not be assigned to individual models by analogy.
cautions: Country-to-model assignment creates an ecological fallacy.
Map positions depend on survey variables and wave.
A model may imitate cultural stereotypes rather than distributions.

ai_evidence.title: WorldValuesBench
ai_evidence.detail: Provides question-level population distributions from which culture-level patterns can be studied without pretending the survey itself is a two-axis model.

hofstede-cultural-dimensions-6.lead: Six country-level dimensions used to describe broad cultural differences, including Power Distance, Individualism, and Uncertainty Avoidance.
hofstede-cultural-dimensions-6.verdict: Widely recognized and directly used in LLM cultural audits, but country scores must never be presented as individual traits.
hofstede-cultural-dimensions-6.measurement: The Value Survey Module and country indices were designed for aggregate comparison. Exact edition, aggregation, reference countries, language, and prompt persona belong in the method.
cautions: Country indices are not individual personality scores.
National averages can encourage essentialism.
An LLM can reproduce a cultural stereotype without matching population variance.

ai_evidence.title: Cultural Alignment in Large Language Models
ai_evidence.detail: Applies a Hofstede Cultural Alignment Test to Llama 2, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 across US, Chinese, and Arab settings and tests prompting and language fine-tuning.

ai_evidence.title: How Well Do LLMs Represent Values Across Cultures?
ai_evidence.detail: Evaluates cultural representation across dimensions, countries, personas, and languages.

globe-cultural-dimensions-9.lead: Nine culture-level dimensions with an unusually valuable distinction between practices—what is—and values—what should be.
globe-cultural-dimensions-9.verdict: The clearest cultural analogue to stated-versus-observed separation; richer than Hofstede for that question, but still aggregate.

scope.evidence: Large cross-cultural organizational program; early AI adoption

globe-cultural-dimensions-9.measurement: Preserve the separate ‘as is’ and ‘should be’ item batteries. Combining both erases the framework’s most informative measurement distinction.
cautions: The unit is a cultural aggregate, not an individual assistant.
Names shared with Hofstede do not imply equivalent measurements.
Nine dimensions require more than one prompt per label.

ai_evidence.title: LLM-GLOBE
ai_evidence.detail: Builds a benchmark around GLOBE cultural values embedded in model outputs, establishing a direct AI operationalization.

rokeach-value-system-36.lead: Thirty-six values split into eighteen desired end states and eighteen preferred modes of conduct, traditionally rank ordered.
rokeach-value-system-36.verdict: Historically foundational and genuinely broad, but its fixed vocabulary and full-ranking task have much thinner modern AI adoption than Schwartz.

scope.evidence: Classic human instrument; sparse direct LLM evidence

rokeach-value-system-36.measurement: The classic task rank-orders two lists. Rating adaptations change the response process: ranks encode order, while ratings also imply magnitude and allow ties.
cautions: Ranks preserve order but not distance.
Forced full ranking magnifies near-ties and order effects.
The vocabulary reflects its historical and cultural context.

ai_evidence.title: Measuring Human-AI Value Alignment in Large Language Models
ai_evidence.detail: Uses a hybrid taxonomy drawing on Rokeach alongside Schwartz, Life Values Inventory, and WVS; it is not a pure Rokeach replication.

social-value-orientation.lead: A focused construct describing how people trade off outcomes for themselves and another person in allocation tasks.
social-value-orientation.verdict: A strong behavioral analogue for conflict choice, but far too narrow to serve as a complete value profile.

scope.evidence: Established behavioral measure; little direct LLM validation

social-value-orientation.measurement: The SVO Slider Measure estimates an angle from repeated allocation choices. A single dilemma or a verbal claim of altruism is not an SVO score.
cautions: SVO covers allocation, not broad human values.
Hypothetical and incentivized choices can differ.
Framing, recipient identity, and payoff ranges can shift choices.

ai_evidence.title: Current evidence gap
ai_evidence.detail: The literature contains many multi-agent and social-preference tasks, but no comparably established LLM measurement line that validates the canonical SVO Slider as a stable model construct.

functional-theory-human-values-18.lead: Eighteen marker values form six subfunctions by crossing goal orientation—personal, central, social—with motivator—materialistic or humanitarian.
functional-theory-human-values-18.verdict: The most structured broad human-theory alternative to Schwartz for a robustness study; direct LLM validation is still a clear research gap.

scope.evidence: Validated human theory; nearly absent as an LLM benchmark

functional-theory-human-values-18.measurement: BVS-18 estimates Excitement, Promotion, Existence, Suprapersonal, Interactive, and Normative subfunctions. The 2×3 structure should survive aggregation and cross-framework analysis.
uses: Testing whether LLM structure is theory-dependent
cautions: The six subfunctions are not Schwartz-4 under new names.
Lexical crosswalks require empirical validation.
Limited LLM adoption means new results would be novel but less directly comparable.

ai_evidence.title: Direct LLM benchmark gap
ai_evidence.detail: No dedicated, widely used LLM benchmark based on the full Functional Theory was identified in the current corpus; this is a substantive opportunity, not evidence of inferiority.

gpla-five-factor.lead: Five interpretable factors induced from 123 atomic values measured across LLM outputs with a generative psycho-lexical pipeline.
gpla-five-factor.verdict: The strongest named LLM-native competitor to Schwartz, with promising predictive validation but only one young construction lineage.

scope.evidence: Peer-reviewed AI-native construction; limited independent replication

gpla-five-factor.measurement: A Perception Parser extracts value-laden propositions, a Value Generator proposes atomic values, and a Value Evaluator scores them before factor analysis induces broader dimensions.
uses: Full named robustness space for LLMs
LLM value alignment and factor-profile comparison
cautions: Factors depend on model panel, term bank, prompts, parser, and evaluator.
Labels interpret loading patterns rather than discover timeless categories.
Reported superiority to Schwartz is task- and construction-specific until independently replicated.

ai_evidence.title: Generative Psycho-Lexical Approach for Constructing Value Systems in LLMs
ai_evidence.detail: Reports better fit and 87±9% safety-prediction accuracy versus 81±15% for Schwartz-4 and 74±16% for Schwartz-10 baselines in its setup.

univar-latent-value-space.lead: A high-dimensional encoder learned from value-relevant question–answer sets, designed to compare model–language patterns without fixed named axes.
univar-latent-value-space.verdict: Powerful for identity, clustering, and cross-lingual similarity; unsuitable when the result must say which named value increased.

scope.evidence: Peer-reviewed AI-native method; one main lineage

univar-latent-value-space.measurement: The encoder maps sets of value-eliciting answers to a dense representation. Comparison uses distance, clustering, or downstream probes—not direct interpretation of coordinate 17 or 83.
uses: Latent robustness check alongside named spaces
cautions: Coordinates have no stable named meaning.
A 2D plot is only a projection.
Distance inherits the elicitation bank and contrastive training objective.

ai_evidence.title: High-Dimension Human Value Representation in Large Language Models
ai_evidence.detail: Learns from 8 source LLMs and evaluates 15 open and commercial LLMs across 25 languages and cultures.

value-kaleidoscope-ontology.lead: A contextual ontology connects values, rights, duties, situations, valence, and stakeholders instead of forcing all evidence into one global vector.
value-kaleidoscope-ontology.verdict: Best fit for explaining contextual L2/L3 conflicts; complementary to—not a replacement for—a stable model-level profile.

scope.construct: Contextually relevant values, rights, and duties
scope.evidence: Peer-reviewed resource with human acceptance validation

value-kaleidoscope-ontology.measurement: Relevant concepts are generated and linked to situations with support, opposition, or ambiguity. The result is relational and contextual rather than one normalized profile.
uses: Audit L2 choice and L3 framing
cautions: Contextual relevance is not global endorsement.
An ontology is not automatically a numeric profile.
Generated concepts and relations still require coverage and quality audits.

ai_evidence.title: Value Kaleidoscope: Engaging AI with Pluralistic Human Values, Rights, and Duties
ai_evidence.detail: Introduces the contextual ontology and ValuePrism resource, with reported 91% human acceptance of generated concepts.

hhh-principles.lead: Helpful, Honest, and Harmless are broad assistant objectives used in training and evaluation—not a comprehensive descriptive theory of values.
hhh-principles.verdict: Useful policy shorthand and evaluation target; too underspecified to serve as a value ontology without task rubrics and conflict rules.
hhh-principles.measurement: Each objective needs task definitions, preference data, rubrics, or evaluators. The words themselves do not specify trade-offs when helpfulness conflicts with harmlessness or honesty.
cautions: HHH is prescriptive, not a measured latent profile.
Objectives conflict in concrete cases.
Evaluator and policy choices determine the effective meaning.

ai_evidence.title: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment
ai_evidence.detail: Operationalizes helpful, honest, and harmless behavior through preference-modeling and assistant evaluation experiments.

constitutional-principle-space.lead: A configurable collection of natural-language principles used to critique, revise, and prefer model outputs.
constitutional-principle-space.verdict: A steering mechanism and policy artifact, not evidence of a model’s intrinsic or stable values.
constitutional-principle-space.measurement: Constitution text, critique prompt, revision prompt, preference-model procedure, and training stage jointly define the operational target.
cautions: A constitution declares desired behavior; it does not reveal latent identity.
Changing principles changes the target.
Compliance depends on evaluator interpretation and conflict resolution.

ai_evidence.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
ai_evidence.detail: Introduces supervised self-critique/revision followed by reinforcement learning from AI feedback under a written principle set.

gpv-open-value-space.lead: GPV separates text into value-laden perceptions and evaluates dynamically supplied values, so it is a measurement pipeline rather than one fixed axiology.
gpv-open-value-space.verdict: The most relevant open-vocabulary scoring design for free text; it still needs an explicit value list or ontology and a validated evaluator.
gpv-open-value-space.measurement: First split long outputs into atomic perceptions without changing meaning; then score every relevant perception against supplied value definitions. Aggregation, zero-evidence, contradiction, and coverage rules determine the final profile.
uses: Mapping one response into multiple named spaces
cautions: GPV is not itself a five- or ten-value ontology.
A parser can lose negation, speaker attribution, or context.
Scores from separately prompted values may not share a calibrated scale.

ai_evidence.title: Measuring Human and AI Values Based on Generative Psychometrics
ai_evidence.detail: Formalizes perception extraction before value evaluation and supports supplied value concepts beyond a single fixed theory.

ai_evidence.title: GPLA
ai_evidence.detail: Reuses the perception-parser idea as the first stage of constructing an LLM-native value system, showing that parsing and axiology construction are distinct steps.
